title: Pussy Pussy Pussy and the jukebox hit with Gin Mill Blues on the back
summary: Parker recalls the notorious record with Gin Mill Blues on the B side. It sold enormously in jukeboxes, and he thinks it should be reissued.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. And we were doing the first Dirty Merrick's, but we got by with it first, and then they became dirtier and dirtier. It's amazing.
And you never changed your name on those?

No. No. I told you on this one, this is interesting. This, uh, Tien Collin, this is really, the title is Pussy Pussy Pussy. And, uh, there was a refrain that was unmistakable as to, uh, symbolism. And on the back then, we wanted to put something that would be a little bit better, higher status. And we had a good arrangement of Gin Mill Blues, so that was what we put on the back, the B side of it was Gin Mill Blues, which we thought wouldn't sell anyway. I mean, it didn't really. Nothing, nothing could compete with that, any side of that record ever. And, uh, it did sell enormously in the jukeboxes. It went over, people would see that name there, and this is enough for a nickel any time. They should re-release that thing.
